title: Solve two-step equations in other forms: x/3 + 5 = 2 and 2(x + 4) = −6

lesson.title: Two-Step Equations in Disguise

steps.say: You already crush equations like negative four x plus seven equals nineteen. Today x shows up dressed differently — divided by three, or trapped inside brackets — but the exact same two moves still work.

Think of the equation as a balance scale. Whatever is stuck to x from the outside comes off first. In x divided by three plus five, the plus five is on the outside, so it goes first. And the golden rule: whatever you do, you do it to the whole side, not just one piece.

visual.caption: Both sides balance — keep them equal at every step

steps.say: Let us do it. Subtract five from both sides: two minus five is negative three, so x divided by three equals negative three. Now undo the divide by three by multiplying both sides by three: negative three times three is negative nine. So x equals negative nine. Check it: negative nine divided by three is negative three, and negative three plus five is two. It works.

Now the bracket one. Two times the bracket equals negative six, so first divide both sides by two: the bracket x plus four equals negative three. Then subtract four from both sides: negative three minus four is negative seven. So x equals negative seven. Check: negative seven plus four is negative three, and two times negative three is negative six. Perfect.

visual.caption: Halve both sides and the scale stays level

steps.say: Here are the two traps. Trap one: multiplying by three but only touching one term, turning x divided by three plus five equals two into x plus five equals six. That is broken — the three has to hit every single term, including the five and the two. Trap two: distributing to only the first term, writing two x plus four instead of two x plus eight. Both mistakes tip the scale over.

visual.caption: Touching only one term breaks the balance

steps.say: So remember: work from the outside in. Undo the plus or minus first, then the multiply or divide — and whatever you do, do it to the entire side.

lesson.answer: Peel from the outside in — and whatever you do, do it to every term on both sides.

practice.question: Grab a pencil and solve this one: two times, open bracket, x plus six, close bracket, equals negative ten. Divide both sides by two first, then undo the inside. What is x? Bonus: check your answer by putting it back in.
practice.answer: x equals negative eleven. Dividing both sides by two gives x plus six equals negative five, then subtracting six gives x equals negative eleven. Check: negative eleven plus six is negative five, and two times negative five is negative ten.
